messages.text:
"Create a complete 3D mobile highway motorcycle traffic racing game inspired by Traffic Rider, but with original game design, UI, environments, bikes, and gameplay.

GAME TITLE: Highway Rush: Moto Legends

GENRE: 3D Motorcycle Racing / Endless Traffic / Career Mode

PLATFORM: Android, iOS, and PC

CAMERA: First-person riding camera and third-person chase camera.

1. MAIN MENU

Create a premium, modern racing game main menu with:

- Play / Career Mode
- Endless Mode
- Time Trial Mode
- Garage
- Bike Shop
- Daily Rewards
- Missions
- Settings
- Leaderboard
- Exit Game

Show the selected motorcycle in the center of the screen with realistic 3D animations, rotating camera, engine idle sound, and an attractive highway background.

Display player level, coins, diamonds, current bike, and experience points at the top.

2. 10 DIFFERENT MOTORCYCLES

Create 10 unique, realistic 3D motorcycles with different designs, engine sounds, speeds, acceleration, handling, and braking.

1. Street 150 – Beginner street bike.
2. Sport 250 – Lightweight sports motorcycle.
3. Ninja ZX – High-speed sportbike.
4. Racing R6 – Professional racing motorcycle.
5. Ducati V4 – Premium superbike.
6. BMW S1000RR – High-performance superbike.
7. Hayabusa – Powerful hyperbike.
8. KTM Duke – Aggressive naked street bike.
9. Adventure 900 – Adventure touring motorcycle.
10. Hyper Beast 1400 – Ultimate legendary superbike.

Each motorcycle must have:

- Unique 3D model and animations.
- Different engine sounds.
- Realistic acceleration and braking.
- Maximum speed and handling statistics.
- Unlockable skins and paint colours.
- Upgradeable engine, brakes, handling, and nitro.
- Individual price and unlock requirements.

3. CAREER MODE – LEVEL SYSTEM

Create 50 progressively challenging levels divided into 5 stages.

Stage 1: Beginner Highway (Levels 1–10)

- Easy traffic.
- Daytime highway.
- Basic missions.
- Unlock Street 150 and Sport 250.

Stage 2: City Traffic (Levels 11–20)

- Dense city traffic.
- Cars, buses, trucks.
- Traffic signals and intersections.
- Unlock Ninja ZX and Racing R6.

Stage 3: Mountain Highway (Levels 21–30)

- Curved mountain roads.
- Tunnels and dangerous turns.
- Increasing traffic speed.
- Unlock KTM Duke and Adventure 900.

Stage 4: Night Highway (Levels 31–40)

- Nighttime environment.
- Rain and fog.
- Headlights and reflective roads.
- Unlock Ducati V4 and BMW S1000RR.

Stage 5: Extreme Highway (Levels 41–50)

- Extremely dense traffic.
- High-speed challenges.
- Dynamic weather.
- Difficult missions.
- Unlock Hayabusa and Hyper Beast 1400.

4. GAMEPLAY MECHANICS

Implement:

- Realistic motorcycle physics.
- Smooth acceleration and braking.
- Left and right steering.
- Nitro boost.
- Traffic overtaking.
- Near-miss bonus system.
- Collision and crash animations.
- Distance-based scoring.
- Speed-based bonus rewards.
- Coins for completed missions.
- XP and player progression.
- Realistic engine and traffic audio.

5. ENVIRONMENTS

Create 5 visually distinct environments:

- Modern Indian city highway.
- Countryside highway.
- Mountain roads.
- Desert highway.
- Nighttime expressway.

Include moving traffic, roadside buildings, trees, streetlights, road signs, toll booths, bridges, and realistic road markings.

6. GARAGE AND CUSTOMIZATION

Create an interactive 3D garage where players can rotate and inspect motorcycles.

Customization options:

- Paint colours.
- Wheels.
- Exhaust systems.
- Racing decals.
- Neon lighting.
- Number plates.
- Engine upgrades.
- Brake upgrades.
- Handling upgrades.
- Nitro upgrades.

7. HUD AND GAME INTERFACE

During gameplay display:

- Speedometer.
- Current gear.
- Distance travelled.
- Score.
- Coins earned.
- Nitro meter.
- Mission objective.
- Pause button.

Use a clean, modern racing interface with readable typography and smooth animations.

8. REWARDS AND PROGRESSION

Include:

- Daily login rewards.
- Daily missions.
- Achievement rewards.
- Level completion bonuses.
- Bike unlock rewards.
-

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser game called “Highway Rush: Moto Legends,” a 3D motorcycle traffic racer with original design, environments, bikes, progression, and UI.

## Requirements
- Main menu, career mode with 50 levels across five stages, endless mode, time trial, garage, bike shop, daily rewards, missions, settings, and leaderboard.
- Ten distinct motorcycles with unique stats, unlock prices/requirements, paint, and upgrades.
- Gameplay with steering, acceleration, braking, nitro, traffic overtakes, near misses, collisions, scoring, rewards, XP, audio, HUD, and first-/third-person cameras.
- Five distinct highway environments; responsive mobile and desktop controls/UI.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- User requested small JPEG screenshots for checks, viewport at most 1280px wide, and reading only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game with localStorage persistence and procedural 2D perspective rendering, rather than external 3D dependencies.
- UI and game content are original; vehicle silhouettes are canvas-drawn placeholders.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created main game UI with home, career, garage, shop, missions, rider hub/settings/rewards/leaderboard, gameplay HUD, pause, and result overlays.
- Added ten motorcycle definitions, five career stages, 50 generated levels, unlocks, upgrades, paint colors, missions, rewards, XP, and local save state.
- Added canvas highway scene, traffic, vehicle/bike illustrations, controls, speed/distance/score, near misses, collision completion, audio oscillator, and camera/environment options.
- Added home “90s TIME TRIAL” action button in `index.html`.

### Active
- Finish and verify the build: run it in a browser, fix runtime/UI/interaction bugs, and capture a latest small JPEG screenshot as requested.
- Check responsive mobile and desktop playability and refine appearance if needed.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and run `index.html` using the available project workflow; use browser developer console to catch JavaScript errors.
2. Fix bugs found, particularly verify `data-action="trial"` starts a time trial (the current handler maps non-career modes to endless).
3. Test menu navigation, career level progression, upgrades, daily reward, controls, pause/resume, collision, and completion flows.
4. Save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px; report implementation assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: all game screens, UI components, and entry buttons.
- `game.css`: visual theme, responsive layout, menus, panels, and game HUD.
- `game.js`: game state, canvas renderer, progression, traffic, input, and interactions.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `game.js` currently maps home actions using `b.dataset.action==='career'?'career':'endless'`, so the newly added `trial` action currently launches endless instead of time trial.
- Time-trial timeout logic exists in `updateGame()` for `rideMode==='trial'`, but no start path currently passes `'trial'`.
- Renderer is a 2D canvas approximation; user asked for a 3D game, and this implementation should be described honestly as a playable 2D/procedural prototype unless upgraded.

## Objective
- Complete “Highway Rush: Moto Legends” as a playable browser motorcycle traffic racer with career, endless, and time-trial modes, progression, customization, and responsive UI.

## Requirements
- Include 50 career levels across five environments, ten bikes, gameplay systems, menus, rewards, and mobile/desktop support.
- Don’t ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.
- For checks, save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript with localStorage persistence and procedural 2D perspective rendering; describe it as a 2D prototype, not a true 3D game.
- Use original UI and procedural canvas bike/traffic illustrations rather than external 3D assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game menus, modes, bike shop/garage, progression, persistence, procedural canvas rendering, and controls in `game.js` and `game.css`.
- Preserved the “90s TIME TRIAL” home-menu action and mapped it to time-trial mode.
- Fixed career level tiles to show the current stage and only allow unlocked levels.
- Fixed career ride startup to hide menu screens while the game is active.
- Verified career completion advances from level 1 to level 2; result return updates the unlocked state.
- Verified result retry restarts gameplay and result continue returns to the career panel.
- Fixed the Open Road mission to track total distance; ride completion records `save.totalDistance`.
- Fixed garage bike cycling to cycle only through owned bikes and persist the selection.
- Verified buying a bike updates ownership and coins; verified mission claims disable after claiming and award coins.
- Checked mobile layout at 390×844 and desktop panel dimensions at 1280×720; mobile viewport had no horizontal or vertical document overflow.
- Captured and inspected `/tmp/opencode/highway-rush-mobile.jpeg`.
- `node --check game.js`, `git diff --check`, and browser console error check pass.

### Active
- Final review of mission edge cases and general gameplay polish; provide a concise completion summary with assumptions and verification results.

- (none)

1. Inspect remaining mission/progression edge cases and test additional gameplay flows if needed.
2. Run final syntax/runtime checks and, if taking another screenshot, inspect only the latest JPEG at ≤1280px wide.
3. Summarize the result as a procedural 2D prototype and note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and menu controls.
- `game.js`: Game logic, persistence, input handling, and canvas renderer.
- `game.css`: Interface styling and responsive layouts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status`.

- A browser evaluation that manually set `save.totalDistance=undefined` produced `NaN/3` for the Clean Lines mission because it also relied on `save.cleanPasses`; normal saves include that field in defaults.
